title: Startups are emotionally draining: how to get through the urge to quit
summary: Jason Cohen argues most small startups fail because founders stop, often from emotional exhaustion. He tells how a bullying enterprise procurement manager made him want to quit, even though the man had no real power. His point: you don't need to be stoic or confident, just keep going.

principles.text: Most small startups fail because the founders stop working on them, often from emotional drain.
principles.quote: Most startups fail "only" because the founders stop working on them, and often it's because it's emotionally draining.

principles.text: Emotional lows are not just an early-stage problem; they persist years later despite revenue, profit and a great team.
principles.quote: The pain is not limited to the beginning of the venture. It's still there years later, despite real revenue, profitability, customers arriving every day, and a great team.

principles.text: Surviving a startup doesn't require constant confidence, stoicism or wisdom; it requires sticking through the tough parts despite your weaknesses.
principles.quote: Getting through this slog of a thing that's a startup--or anything difficult and worthwhile--doesn't require that you're always confident or stoic or smart or right or wise.

principles.text: Aim to live through hard emotional moments rather than beat them; reasoning often never erases the feeling.
principles.quote: Living through it, not beating it.

principles.text: Publish prices on your website and don't discount, even in enterprise deals; bulk pricing is already built in.
principles.quote: We don't discount; instead we put our pricing on our website so there's no misunderstanding.

principles.text: Stopping is the real way little startups fail, so tenacity matters even if it isn't all it takes.
principles.quote: I'm not saying tenacity is all it takes. Just that without it, you'll stop.
